extracted.intended_audience: practitioners before the USPTO (registered patent attorneys and agents) and lawyers comparing ABA Model Rules to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Extract and apply the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct (mapped to ABA Model Rules) governing ethical behavior of practitioners representing clients before the Office, including responsibilities of prosecutors, advertising, communications, supervisory duties, pro bono, conflicts, and practice restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3.8 Special Responsibilities Of A Prosecutor
rubrics_metrics.description: The prosecutor in a criminal case shall: (a) refrain from prosecuting a charge that the prosecutor knows is not supported by probable cause; (b) make reasonable efforts to assure that the accused has been advised of the right to, and the procedure for obtaining, counsel and has been given reasonable opportunity to obtain counsel; (c) not seek to obtain from an unrepresented accused a waiver of important pretrial rights; (d) make timely disclosure to the defense of all evidence or information known to the prosecutor that tends to negate the guilt of the accused or mitigates the offense, and in connection with sentencing disclose all unprivileged mitigating information known to the prosecutor except when relieved by a protective order; (e) not subpoena a lawyer in a grand jury or other criminal proceeding to present evidence about a past or present client unless prosecutor reasonably believes (1) the information sought is not privileged, (2) the evidence is essential to successful completion of an investigation or prosecution, and (3) there is no other feasible alternative; (f) except for statements necessary to inform the public of the nature and extent of the prosecutor's action and that serve a legitimate law enforcement purpose, refrain from making extrajudicial comments likely to heighten public condemnation of the accused and exercise reasonable care to prevent others assisting the prosecutor from making prohibited extrajudicial statements; (g) when knowing of new, credible and material evidence creating a reasonable likelihood that a convicted defendant did not commit the offense, promptly disclose it to an appropriate court or authority and, if conviction was in prosecutor's jurisdiction, disclose to the defendant unless court authorizes delay and undertake or cause further investigation; (h) when knowing of clear and convincing evidence that a defendant in prosecutor's jurisdiction was convicted of an offense the defendant did not commit, seek to remedy the conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains enumerated duties and exceptions (e.g., protective orders, privilege), and specific standards for when subpoenas of lawyers are permissible and for post-conviction disclosure and remedial obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3.9 Advocate In Nonadjudicative Proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner representing a client before a legislative body or administrative agency in a nonadjudicative proceeding shall disclose that the appearance is in a representative capacity and shall conform to the provisions of §§ 11.303(a)–(c), 11.304(a)–(c), and 11.305.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires disclosure of representative capacity and compliance with specified rules (cross-references to rules on candor, fairness, and communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4.1 Truthfulness In Statements To Others
rubrics_metrics.description: In the course of representing a client, a practitioner shall not knowingly: (a) make a false statement of material fact or law to a third person; or (b) fail to disclose a material fact to a third person when disclosure is necessary to avoid assisting a criminal or fraudulent act by a client, unless disclosure is prohibited by § 11.106.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to statements of both fact and law and includes an exception where disclosure is prohibited by confidentiality rules; mirrors ABA standard but cites USPTO-specific confidentiality cross-reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4.2 Communication With Person Represented By Counsel
rubrics_metrics.description: In representing a client, a practitioner shall not communicate about the subject of the representation with a person the practitioner knows to be represented by another practitioner in the matter, unless the practitioner has the consent of the other practitioner or is authorized to do so by law, rule, or a court order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes an explicit exception for communications with government officials who are otherwise represented but have authority to redress grievances, provided the practitioner first discloses their identity and that they represent a party with a claim against the government (see attached disclosure language).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4.3 Dealing With Unrepresented Person
rubrics_metrics.description: In dealing on behalf of a client with a person who is not represented by counsel, a practitioner shall not state or imply that the practitioner is disinterested. When the practitioner knows or reasonably should know that the unrepresented person misunderstands the practitioner’s role, the practitioner shall make reasonable efforts to correct the misunderstanding. The practitioner shall not give legal advice to an unrepresented person, other than the advice to secure counsel, if the practitioner knows or reasonably should know that the interests of such a person are or have a reasonable possibility of being in conflict with the interests of the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires active correction of role misunderstandings and forbids giving substantive legal advice to unrepresented persons where a conflict exists or may reasonably arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4.4 Respect For Rights Of Third Persons
rubrics_metrics.description: In representing a client, a practitioner shall not use means that have no substantial purpose other than to embarrass, delay, or burden a third person, or use methods of obtaining evidence that violate the legal rights of such a person. A practitioner who receives a document or electronically stored information relating to the representation of the practitioner’s client and knows or reasonably should know that the document or electronically stored information was inadvertently sent shall promptly notify the sender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits abusive or legally improper evidence-gathering tactics and imposes a duty to notify upon receipt of inadvertently sent materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5.1 Responsibilities Of Partners, Managers, And Supervisory Practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner who is a partner in a law firm, and a practitioner who individually or together with other practitioners possesses comparable managerial authority in a law firm, shall make reasonable efforts to ensure that the firm has in effect measures giving reasonable assurance that all practitioners in the firm conform to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct. (b) A practitioner having direct supervisory authority over another practitioner shall make reasonable efforts to ensure that the other practitioner conforms to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct. (c) A practitioner shall be responsible for another practitioner’s violation of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct if (1) the practitioner orders or, with knowledge of the specific conduct, ratifies the conduct involved; or (2) the practitioner is a partner or has comparable managerial authority or direct supervisory authority in the firm, knows of the conduct at a time when its consequences can be avoided or mitigated but fails to take reasonable remedial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes supervisory and managerial duties to implement measures ensuring compliance and spells out when supervisors and partners may be held responsible for subordinate misconduct (ordering/ratifying or knowing and failing to remediate).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5.2 Responsibilities Of A Subordinate Practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner is bound by the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct notwithstanding that the practitioner acted at the direction of another person. (b) A subordinate practitioner does not violate the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct if that practitioner acts in accordance with a supervisory practitioner’s reasonable resolution of an arguable question of professional duty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subordinates remain bound by the rules but have a defense when they follow a supervisory practitioner's reasonable resolution of an arguable professional duty question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5.3 Responsibilities Regarding Non-Practitioner Assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: With respect to a non-practitioner assistant employed or retained by or associated with a practitioner: (a) partners and those with managerial authority shall make reasonable efforts to ensure the firm has measures giving reasonable assurance that the person's conduct is compatible with the professional obligations of the practitioner; (b) a practitioner having direct supervisory authority over the non-practitioner assistant shall make reasonable efforts to ensure the person’s conduct is compatible with the practitioner’s professional obligations; and (c) a practitioner shall be responsible for conduct of such a person that would be a violation of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct if engaged in by a practitioner if (1) the practitioner orders or, with knowledge of the specific conduct, ratifies the conduct involved; or (2) the practitioner is a partner or has comparable managerial authority or direct supervisory authority and knows of the conduct when its consequences can be avoided or mitigated but fails to take reasonable remedial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extends supervisory obligations and potential liability to non-practitioner staff and assistants; emphasizes implementing firm measures to ensure compatible conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5.4 Professional Independence Of A Practitioner
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner or law firm shall not share legal fees with a non-practitioner, except limited exceptions (payments to estate, purchase of practice, inclusion of non-practitioner employees in compensation/retirement plans, sharing with qualifying nonprofit organizations). (b) A practitioner shall not form a partnership with a non-practitioner if any of the activities of the partnership consist of the practice of law. (c) A practitioner shall not permit a person who recommends, employs, or pays the practitioner to render legal services for another to direct or regulate the practitioner’s professional judgment in rendering such legal services. (d) A practitioner shall not practice with or in the form of a professional corporation or association authorized to practice law for a profit if a non-practitioner owns any interest therein (subject to estate fiduciary exception), is a corporate director/officer, or has the right to direct or control the practitioner’s professional judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects professional independence by restricting fee-sharing, business structures, outside control, and non-practitioner ownership or management that could influence professional judgment; lists enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5.5 Unauthorized Practice Of Law; Multijurisdictional Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner shall not practice law in a jurisdiction in violation of the regulation of the legal profession in that jurisdiction, or assist another in doing so. (b) A practitioner who is not admitted in this jurisdiction shall not, except as authorized by the Rules or other law, establish an office or systematic and continuous presence in this jurisdiction for the practice of law or hold out that the practitioner is admitted in this jurisdiction. (c) A practitioner admitted in another U.S. jurisdiction and not disbarred or suspended may provide temporary legal services in this jurisdiction under specified conditions (association with admitted practitioner who actively participates; services reasonably related to pending or potential proceedings; arbitration/mediation-related services arising out of practice in admitted jurisdiction and not requiring pro hac vice; other services reasonably related to practice). (d) A practitioner admitted in another U.S. jurisdiction may provide legal services that are provided to the practitioner's employer or affiliates and are not services for which the forum requires pro hac vice admission, or services authorized by federal or other law of the jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines when out-of-jurisdiction practitioners may lawfully provide services and cautions against establishing an unauthorized presence or misrepresenting admission status; enumerates limited exceptions and conditions for temporary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5.6 Restrictions On Right To Practice
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not participate in offering or making: (a) a partnership, shareholders, operating, employment, or other similar agreement that restricts the right of a practitioner to practice after termination of the relationship, except an agreement concerning benefits upon retirement; or (b) an agreement in which a restriction on the practitioner’s right to practice is part of the settlement of a client controversy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits contractual restraints on future practice except limited retirement-benefit arrangements, and forbids using such restrictions as settlement terms in client controversies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5.7 Responsibilities Regarding Law-Related Services
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner shall be subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct with respect to the provision of law-related services if the law-related services are provided (1) by the practitioner in circumstances that are not distinct from the practitioner’s provision of legal services to clients; or (2) in other circumstances by an entity controlled by the practitioner individually or with others if the practitioner fails to take reasonable measures to assure that a person obtaining the law-related services knows that the services are not legal services and that the protections of the client-practitioner relationship do not exist. (b) The term “law-related services” denotes services that might reasonably be performed in conjunction with and in substance are related to the provision of legal services, and that are not prohibited as unauthorized practice of law when provided by a nonlawyer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects law-related services to professional rules when the services are not distinct from legal services or when the practitioner does not adequately inform consumers that protections differ; defines scope of 'law-related services.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6.1 Voluntary Pro Bono Publico Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Every lawyer has a professional responsibility to provide legal services to those unable to pay. A lawyer should aspire to render at least fifty (50) hours of pro bono publico legal services per year. In fulfilling this responsibility, the lawyer should: (a) provide a substantial majority of the (50) hours without fee or expectation of fee to (1) persons of limited means or (2) charitable, religious, civic, community, governmental and educational organizations in matters designed primarily to address the needs of persons of limited means; and (b) provide any additional services through (1) delivery of legal services at no fee or substantially reduced fee to individuals, groups or organizations seeking to secure or protect civil rights, civil liberties or public rights, or qualifying organizations; (2) delivery of legal services at a substantially reduced fee to persons of limited means; or (3) participation in activities for improving the law, the legal system or the legal profession. In addition, a lawyer should voluntarily contribute financial support to organizations that provide legal services to persons of limited means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets aspirational benchmark (50 hours) and indicates priority categories for pro bono work and permissible forms of contribution (time, reduced-fee work, systemic activities, financial support).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6.2 Accepting Appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not seek to avoid appointment by a tribunal to represent a person except for good cause, such as: (a) representing the client is likely to result in violation of the Rules of Professional Conduct or other law; (b) representing the client is likely to result in an unreasonable financial burden on the practitioner; or (c) the client or the cause is so repugnant to the practitioner as to be likely to impair the client-practitioner relationship or the practitioner’s ability to represent the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires acceptance of court appointments absent specified grounds for recusal or refusal; grounds focus on ethical conflicts, undue burden, or integrity impairment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6.3 Membership In Legal Services Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may serve as a director, officer or member of a legal services organization, apart from the law firm in which the practitioner practices, notwithstanding that the organization serves persons having interests adverse to a client of the practitioner. The practitioner shall not knowingly participate in a decision or action of the organization: (a) if participating in the decision or action would be incompatible with the practitioner's obligations to a client under Rule 1.7; or (b) where the decision or action could have a material adverse effect on the representation of a client of the organization whose interests are adverse to a client of the practitioner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits service in legal services organizations but requires avoidance of participation in decisions creating conflicts with the practitioner's client obligations or materially adverse effects on client representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6.4 Law Reform Activities Affecting Client Interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may serve as a director, officer or member of an organization involved in reform of the law or its administration notwithstanding that the reform may affect the interests of a client of the practitioner. When the practitioner knows that the interests of a client may be materially benefitted by a decision in which the practitioner participates, the practitioner shall disclose that fact but need not identify the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows participation in law reform while requiring disclosure when a client's interests may materially benefit from a decision; client identity need not be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6.5 Nonprofit And Court-Annexed Limited Legal Services Programs
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner who, under the auspices of a program sponsored by a nonprofit organization or court, provides short-term limited legal services to a client without expectation by either the practitioner or the client that the practitioner will provide continuing representation in the matter: (1) is subject to Rules 1.7 and 1.9(a) only if the practitioner knows that the representation of the client involves a conflict of interest; and (2) is subject to Rule 1.10 only if the practitioner knows that another practitioner associated with the practitioner in a law firm is disqualified by Rule 1.7 or 1.9(a) with respect to the matter. (b) Except as provided in paragraph (a)(2), Rule 1.10 is inapplicable to a representation governed by this Rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides limited conflict-of-interest rules for short-term limited-scope pro bono programs; relaxes certain imputation rules except where the practitioner actually knows of disqualifying conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7.1 Communications Concerning A Practitioner’s Services
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not make a false or misleading communication about the practitioner or the practitioner’s services. A communication is false or misleading if it contains a material misrepresentation of fact or law, or omits a fact necessary to make the statement considered as a whole not materially misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the baseline prohibition on false or materially misleading statements in advertising and other communications; cross-references to advertising and solicitation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7.2 Advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to the requirements of §§ 11.701 and 11.703, a practitioner may advertise services through written, recorded or electronic communication, including public media. A practitioner shall not give anything of value to a person for recommending the practitioner’s services except that a practitioner may: (1) pay the reasonable costs of advertisements or communications permitted by this section; (2) [Reserved]; (3) pay for a law practice in accordance with § 11.117; and (4) refer clients to another practitioner or a non-practitioner professional pursuant to an agreement not otherwise prohibited under the USPTO Rules that provides for reciprocal referrals if (i) the reciprocal referral agreement is not exclusive, and (ii) the client is informed of the existence and nature of the agreement. Any communication made pursuant to this section shall include the name and office address of at least one practitioner or law firm responsible for its content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits advertising subject to truthfulness and solicitation rules, limits fee-sharing/recommendation payments to specific exceptions, requires disclosure of reciprocal referral arrangements and identification of responsible practitioner and address on communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7.3 Direct Contact With Prospective Clients
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner shall not by in-person, live telephone or real-time electronic contact solicit professional employment from a prospective client when a significant motive is pecuniary gain, unless the person contacted is a practitioner or has a family, close personal, or prior professional relationship with the practitioner. (b) A practitioner shall not solicit professional employment from a prospective client by written, recorded or electronic communication or by in-person, telephone or real-time electronic contact if (1) the prospective client has made known a desire not to be solicited or (2) the solicitation involves coercion, duress or harassment. (c) Every written, recorded or electronic communication soliciting professional employment from a prospective client known to be in need of legal services in a particular matter shall include the words 'Advertising Material' on the outside envelope, if any, and at the beginning and ending of any recorded or electronic communication, unless the recipient is a practitioner or has the close/family/prior relationship. (d) Notwithstanding paragraph (a), a practitioner may participate with a prepaid or group legal service plan operated by an organization not owned or directed by the practitioner that uses in-person or telephone contact to solicit memberships or subscriptions for the plan from persons who are not known to need legal services in a particular matter covered by the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restricts live solicitation to prevent undue influence, requires labeling of solicitation communications as advertising in many cases, and permits certain prepaid/group plan solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7.4 Communication Of Fields Of Practice And Specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner may communicate the fact that the practitioner does or does not practice in particular fields of law. (b) A registered practitioner who is an attorney may use designations such as 'Patents,' 'Patent Attorney,' 'Patent Lawyer,' 'Registered Patent Attorney,' or similar; a registered practitioner who is not an attorney may use 'Patents,' 'Patent Agent,' 'Registered Patent Agent,' or similar. Unless authorized by § 11.14(b), a registered patent agent shall not hold himself or herself out as being qualified or authorized to practice before the Office in trademark matters or before a court. (d) A practitioner shall not state or imply that a practitioner is certified as a specialist in a particular field of law unless (1) certified by an organization approved by an appropriate state authority or accredited by the ABA, and (2) the name of the certifying organization is clearly identified in the communication. (e) An individual granted limited recognition under § 11.9 may use the designation 'Limited Recognition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits truthful statements of fields and specific patent-related designations for registered practitioners, but restricts misrepresentations of specialization and cross-practice claims; requires identification of certifying organization when claiming specialist status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7.5 Firm Names And Letterheads
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) A practitioner shall not use a firm name, letterhead or other professional designation that violates § 11.701. A trade name may be used by a practitioner in private practice if it does not imply a connection with a government agency or with a public or charitable legal services organization and is not otherwise in violation of § 11.701. (b) [Reserved].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Controls firm naming and letterhead practices to avoid misleading implications of government affiliation or other material misrepresentations; subject to the baseline communication/truthfulness rule.
